Single-control-plane / multi-data-plane is the active architecture boundary: accounts, orders, artifacts, credential lifecycle, subscription rendering, and usage ledgers stay authoritative in one control store; edge hosts own protocol runtime and traffic capacity only.

Remote data-plane future-order coordination is now coded in source: delivered orders record safe pending desired-state notifications for remote channels, and subscription rendering still requires a matching applied receipt before exposing those channels. The first approved runtime/schema upgrade attempt for edge-agent-future-order-runtime-20260611-001 rolled back safely; a later protected-env normalization gate corrected the earlier shell-source diagnostic and proved EDGE_DATA_PLANE_AGENT_NODES_JSON resolves to an array under a systemd-style parser. The follow-up redacted startup diagnostic found the remaining blocker is Singapore static channel placeholder resolution: the candidate expected a second SGP_* protected material namespace. The repo-only SGP template alignment updated the default/Vultr multichannel templates and tests to use the already approved deployed SGP key names instead, and candidate package edge-agent-future-order-runtime-20260611-002-worktree passed read-only key-presence preflight. Live-order smoke and future-order apply validation still require a separate exact Risk A gate.

Aliyun subscription-distribution records, channel-lab-a/b records, and Japan single-TUIC upgrade records are historical/fallback references. Do not reactivate them as current production authority or automatic issuance targets without a fresh Risk A gate and live verification.

User Portal and Admin/Operator surfaces are adapters over shared domain services. User order creation, lifecycle status, refresh, usage monitor, and support flows must use durable backend state, not frontend Map/demo state.

Order-owned traffic accounting remains an active implementation lane: Admin usage monitor now shows order-owned issued channels from durable state, but live runtime sample collection, User Portal usage display, quota enforcement, and auto-disable still require separate gates.
Legacy query-token retirement remains a separate Risk A lane after opaque artifact coverage, observation, endpoint compatibility checks, rollback evidence, and exact operator approval.

All production/runtime/cloud changes remain Risk A: DNS, Nginx, provider firewall, systemd restarts, runtime config, live order creation, account/password generation, subscription URL/token/password output, and SQLite row dumps stay out of repo-only work.
